label: original-phase input of w/r (and l, x, e, k)
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (99.6% of mass), when the current input token is one of a small letter set: w and r most strongly (rate about 0.38, about 59% of mass together), then l, x, e, k (rate 0.13-0.19), with weaker z and n. Most activations fall on the first occurrence of the token in the sequence (93% of mass). Rate peaks at t=1-3 and drops for late positions. It is essentially silent at the delimiter and during the copy phase. The top activations (near max) are w/r inputs that follow tokens such as j, f, p, 3, c, q, but no single context rule explains which w/r inputs fire: only about 38% of w/r inputs are active, and the preceding-token effects are spread out. The predicate gets most of the mass (dev mass recall 0.91) but precision is only about 0.42.
